text:
mike: Pushed the apples-to-apples loadtest results for mixed sequence lengths + KV-warmup. gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abc123 (raw numbers + config). TL;DR: speculative decoding + int8 quant gave ~1.9x cost reduction on replayed traffic with a ~5% quality delta. synthetic runs show ~2.2x. Looking for quick sanity checks and gating suggestions.
ankita: Nice, thanks. Can you paste the short summary numbers here? hard to open the gist from phone.
perf-bot: Run summary (id: run-2026-03-15-09): model=rwkv-30b-quant-int8, decoding=speculative-1.2, batch_policy=mixed, kv_warmup=enabled, traffic=replay(2026-03-10). cost_delta=-52%, latency_p50=78ms, latency_p95=210ms, quality_metric=qa-accuracy 94.8% (baseline 99.5%).
mike: paste below. baseline is fp16, greedy. important: we ran two controlled variants: (A) replay harness (real traffic) and (B) synthetic steady-state with same seq-length distribution.

mike: Replay: cost -52%, p95 +14ms, qa-accuracy 94.8% (regression 4.7 points)
mike: Synthetic steady-state: cost -57%, p95 +9ms, qa-accuracy 95.1% (regression 4.4 points)

ray: That delta between replay and synthetic is expected if KV warmup behavior differs. Did you separate cold-start vs warmed cache in the replay analysis?
ankita: Good point. How long were sessions in the replay trace? if lots of short sessions, kv cache won't amortize.

mike: Replay trace is 3h of production traffic; median session length ~28 tokens, mean ~62. We included session IDs so we can simulate interrupted sessions. I have a breakdown: cold-session fraction ~38%.
sara: I pushed a small change to kernel-selector last night to favor single-token optimized kernels for seq<=8. Might impact those short sessions; run used previous selector. We should rerun with selector-v2 to compare.
nana: (typo) sorry, ana: can we run a replay where we disable kv_warmup to measure pure cold-cache perf? that will show worst-case latency and quality drift.

mike: Good idea. Suggested next runs: 1) replay with kv_warmup disabled, 2) replay with kernel-selector-v2, 3) run an apples-to-apples with identical batching heuristics but synthetic traffic that mimics session breaks. I'll queue them.
ankita: For gating: propose soft gate at qa-accuracy >=97% relative to baseline and hard gate at >=95%. Also require any cost-optimizing config to have an explicit fallback when qa drops below soft gate.

ray: For apples-to-apples, make sure to pin the kernel and allocator versions. We saw earlier that small libcudnn or kernel tweaks flip the perf/quality curve. Document exact docker image: redwood/infer:2026-03-14-rc3.
perf-bot: enqueued run-2026-03-15-10 (kv_warmup=off), run-2026-03-15-11 (selector=v2). Estimated time ~2.2h each.
mike: Command I used to launch the replay harness (copy/paste):
```
./replay_harness --trace /traces/prod-20260310.json \
  --model rwkv-30b --quant int8 --speculative factor=1.2 \
  --batch-policy mixed --kv-warmup enabled \
  --kernel-selector ref-2026-03-12 --out results/run-2026-03-15
```
ankita: Thanks. Can you also include the prompt/response-length histogram? that will help decide batching thresholds.

mike: pasted short histogram: seq_len_bins: 1-8: 42%, 9-32: 28%, 33-128: 22%, >128:8%
sara: If 42% are <=8, the selector-v2 should help reduce some p95 regressions by using the short-seq kernel. Worth rerunning before deciding on quant/Spec as a ship candidate.
nana: ana: Quick question: how did you measure quality? QA accuracy or human eval?
mike: qa-accuracy is an automated eval over 5k prompt checks we use in regressions. human spot checks done on a 100-sample subset; no catastrophic failures but more truncation artifacts visible with int8+spec.

ray: Suggestion: add a lightweight reranker to the pipeline when using speculative decoding — cheap embed similarity to filter truncated outputs. If it recovers some QA points it's a win.
ankita: Operational ask: please add a regression gate entry in the rollout doc with explicit fallback to fp16 if qa <95% in the first 24h of rollout.

mike: noted. I'll update the rollout doc and rerun with selector-v2 and kv_warmup=off. Will report back when perf-bot posts results. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: run-2026-03-15-10 completed: kv_warmup=off -> cost_delta=-31%, p95=330ms, qa-accuracy=96.2%
perf-bot: run-2026-03-15-11 completed: selector=v2 -> cost_delta=-49%, p95=198ms, qa-accuracy=95.0%

mike: Preliminary take: kv warmup is masking some quality regressions in replay (it lowered p95 but slightly hid truncation behavior). selector-v2 recovered a bunch of latency and kept qa around 95%. Next step: rerun final candidate with short-seq kernels + int8 + speculative but with the reranker patch.
ankita: Sounds good. thanks for owning the runs.
ray: +1. If reranker recovers >=2 pts of QA we can consider a canary.
sara: I'll open a PR for selector-v2 backport to the canary image.
nana: ana: can you add the per-route token-cost breakdown to the results folder? helps billing teams.
keeps: (reaction) :rocket:
